# User description Follow-up to #1952 for the 4.36.0 guided-first-search launch blocker. Production diagnosis - The current production Lambda returns `runtime_evaluation_error`: the five-second local coverage window expires before Manhattan is attempted. - This is not an insufficient-results, insufficient-source-evidence, or Manhattan-coverage miss. Repair - Preserve five seconds of Lambda response headroom while allowing a bounded 16-second evaluation phase. - After a local runtime failure, evaluate one deterministic mission preview in Manhattan. - Never retry private generated query or journey text. - Return Manhattan markers only when the existing editorial/source quality gate passes; otherwise keep `no_qualifying_hero`. Proof - Node 20 targeted ESLint: pass. - 45 adjacent unit/handler tests: pass. - New regressions cover uncovered location -> quality-gated Manhattan ready and weak-evidence refusal. Release order 1. Current-head Baz review and CI clean. 2. Merge this exact fix. 3. Deploy only `onboardingSearchGeneration` to production through the approved deployer. 4. Prove the real production happy, invalid, auth, and safe paths. 5. Only then enable `enable_quiz_guided_first_search_activation`. `mobile_atly_plus_quiz_onboarding` allocation and App Store 4.36.0 are intentionally untouched. --- # Generated description Restore onboardingSearchSelection so local hero evaluation keeps five seconds of Lambda headroom, then retries a single deterministic Manhattan mission preview only after a local runtime failure or timeout. Thread abort and maxTimeMS through onboardingSearchRuntimeCoverage, googlePlaceTypes, placeCategory, and smartSearchV3 so the database-backed coverage lookups stop cleanly during guided onboarding search.

Manhattan rescue Restore the guided onboarding hero flow by extending local evaluation to 16 seconds, then rescuing timed-out runs with one Manhattan mission preview while preserving the quality gate and fail-closed behavior.

meta.title: Restore quality-gated Manhattan rescue for guided onboarding

nodes.body:
### Local timeout can overlap Manhattan work `evaluateAndSelectOnboardingHero` can enter the Manhattan rescue while the previous `evaluateCandidatesWithTimeout(...)` is still running, since the timeout only aborts via `Promise.race([...])` and doesn't wait for the local work to stop; `resolveNearbyLocationsForSearch` and `getCachedActiveGooglePlaceTypesForAtly4` also ignore `signal`, so the bounded-rescue budget can be exceeded — should we thread the abort signal through and wait for the local evaluation to finish cancelling before starting Manhattan? Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz)
Other fix methods
Prompt for AI Agents ```text Before applying, verify this suggestion against the current code. In api/businessLogic/onboardingSearch/onboardingSearchSelection.js around lines 216-296, specifically in evaluateAndSelectOnboardingHero where it sets localEvaluationFailed and then continues into the Manhattan retry when hasMissionPreview is true (lines 257-260 and the subsequent missionPreviewOnly/manhattanGenerationResult construction), fix the “overlapping rescue” behavior. Refactor evaluateCandidatesWithTimeout (or its usage here) so that when a timeout/error occurs it fully cancels the underlying evaluateCandidates work and awaits it to settle before starting Manhattan (do not just return on Promise.race). Also propagate the AbortSignal through the coverage/DB path used by local evaluation (e.g., resolveNearbyLocationsForSearch and getCachedActiveGooglePlaceTypesForAtly4/connectToDatabase/GooglePlaceType.find) so those operations stop when aborted, ensuring the retry budget/bounded rescue behavior is reliable. ```

Commit 85b03fd **addressed** this comment by awaiting the aborted local evaluation before allowing the Manhattan retry to begin. It also propagates the abort signal and query timeout into cached Google place-type lookup and related database operations.

Addressed in 85b03fd04cdca283c489f7ce8f055b80134ffa02. The timeout path now aborts and awaits the local evaluation settlement before Manhattan can start. Cancellation is threaded into active-category and Google-place-type Mongo queries with the existing bounded DB deadline, and the focused regression proves no local/Manhattan overlap.
